name: notification-menu
summary: The interactive header NOTIFICATION panel — a bell + unread-count badge trigger that opens a dropdown with a title, Alerts/System tabs, a scrollable list of notification rows (severity dot + text + time), and a View all / Clear all footer. Self-contained (renders its own trigger + top-layer popover) so it drops into obs-app-header, or stands alone. The turnkey form of the `notification-dropdown` recipe.
selectHint: The header bell + notification panel (alerts/system, badge count)? -> obs-notification-menu in the app-header action area. For a generic action menu use obs-menu; the account dropdown is obs-user-menu.
whenToUse: The top-right notification control of the app shell — the bell with an unread count that opens recent alerts/system notifications with tabs and a scrollable list. One per app chrome.
insteadOf: a hand-built bell + badge + absolutely-positioned panel
obs-menu configured from scratch (this is the turnkey version with tabs + list + footer)
putting notifications in a page instead of the chrome

variants.name: default
variants.what: Bell + badge -> title + Alerts/System tabs + list + View all / Clear all.

variants.name: single-list
variants.what: One tab (or none) -> a flat list with no tab strip.
variants.usage: when there is only one notification stream

variants.name: empty
variants.what: A tab with no items shows a friendly ‘all caught up’ placeholder.

variants.name: severity-coded
variants.what: each row carries a coloured LEFT accent bar from item.severity (--severity-<name>: critical/major/warning/clear/…).
variants.usage: alert streams where severity is the primary signal

variants.name: with-tags
variants.what: rows carry a right-side tag chip (item.tag, via obs-tag) — e.g. Trap / Threshold — to classify the source.
variants.usage: when the notification source/type matters at a glance

variants.name: with-counts
variants.what: tab labels show a count — 'Alerts (191)' / 'System Notification (1822)' — from an explicit tab `count` or computed from items.
variants.usage: the product default; conveys backlog size per stream

variants.name: placement-start
variants.what: placement="bottom-start" aligns the panel to the LEFT of the bell (default is bottom-end / right).
variants.usage: when the bell sits near the right edge’s opposite side

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: bell matches the app-header circular action button; the list scrolls at ~320px max-height.

states.name: open
states.what: the top-layer panel is shown; click-outside / Esc closes it.

states.name: unread
states.what: an unread row gets a subtle --code-tag-background-color highlight.

states.name: empty
states.what: no rows for the active tab -> the placeholder.

count.note: unread count in the badge; 0 hides the badge, >99 shows 99+.

tabs.note: tab labels (comma-list or JSON). JSON items may carry a `count` -> the label shows 'Label (N)' (product: Alerts (191) / System Notification (1822)); else the count is computed from items in that tab. One/zero tabs -> no tab strip.

items.note: notifications: [{tab?, severity?, text, detail?, time?, tag?, unread?}]. `severity` colours the LEFT ACCENT BAR (--severity-<name>); `tag` renders a small chip on the right (e.g. Trap); `time` is a full timestamp on a second line. `detail` is an optional middle line (e.g. an IP).

placement.note: align the panel right (default) or left of the bell.

empty-text.note: placeholder text when a tab has no notifications.

events.name: clear
events.note: Clear all was clicked (for the active tab).

events.name: viewall
events.note: View all was clicked; the consumer navigates to the full page.

decisionFlow: The header bell + notification panel (alerts/system, unread badge)? -> obs-notification-menu, in the obs-app-header action area.
The header account control (avatar -> profile/theme/logout)? -> obs-user-menu, NOT the notification menu.
Streams of different kinds (Alerts vs System)? -> tabs="Alerts,System" and tag each item with a `tab`.
Only one stream? -> tabs="Notifications" (or one label) -> a flat list, no tab strip.
A very long / interactive notification centre? -> open it in an obs-drawer instead (route-away); this element is the compact popover.
Colour a row by severity? -> item.severity (critical/major/warning/clear/up/…) drives the LEFT accent bar via --severity-<name>.
Classify a row's source/type at a glance? -> item.tag renders a right-side chip (Trap / Threshold / Anomaly).
Show backlog size per stream? -> give each tab a `count` (or let it compute from items) → 'Alerts (191)'.
Panel overflowing the right edge? -> placement="bottom-start" anchors it left of the bell.

default.useWhen: the standard header notification dropdown — a bell + badge, Alerts/System tabs, recent items, View all / Clear all
default.dontUse: for a generic action menu (obs-menu) or the account menu (obs-user-menu)
default.example: obs-app-header action area: 3 unread -> Alerts (critical/major/…) + System tabs

single-list.useWhen: there is only one notification stream and tabs add no value
single-list.dontUse: you have genuinely distinct streams (use tabs)

empty.useWhen: always handle the empty state — a tab with no items
empty.dontUse: never leave an empty panel blank

severity-coded.useWhen: the stream is alerts and severity is the primary signal — colour the left accent bar per row
severity-coded.dontUse: purely informational system messages with no severity (leave severity unset → a neutral bar)
severity-coded.example: items=[{severity:'critical', text:'trap alert', …}] → a red left bar

with-tags.useWhen: the source/type of a notification matters at a glance (Trap, Threshold, Anomaly)
with-tags.dontUse: when the title already says it — an extra chip is noise
with-tags.example: items=[{text:'trap alert', tag:'Trap'}] → a small chip on the right

with-counts.useWhen: the product default — show the backlog size on each tab so users see volume before opening
with-counts.dontUse: counts are unknown or misleading (omit the tab `count`)

placement-start.useWhen: the bell is positioned so a right-aligned panel would overflow — anchor it left
placement-start.dontUse: the standard top-right chrome (bottom-end is correct there)

usage.note: One per app shell (the header bell). Turnkey element for the notification-dropdown recipe.

do: Place it in obs-app-header's action area (next to search / before the user menu).
Keep `count` in sync with real unread; wire `clear` + `viewall` to your flows.
Tag each item with a `tab` and a `severity` so it colours + filters correctly.
dont: Don't use it as a generic action menu — that's obs-menu.
Don't cram a full notification centre in the popover — route long/interactive lists to an obs-drawer.
Don't rely on the severity colour alone — the text carries the meaning too.

a11y.summary: The bell is a button with aria-label "Notifications" (include the unread count) + aria-expanded. The panel is a role=dialog; it opens in the top layer and closes on click-outside + Esc. Rows are a list of buttons; severity is conveyed by the dot AND the text, not colour alone.
a11y.notes: Announce new notifications via an aria-live region if the count changes while open. Move focus into the panel on open and back to the bell on close. The tab strip reuses obs-tabs (keyboard-navigable). Ensure the badge count is in the bell's accessible name (e.g. "Notifications, 3 unread").

knownIssues: The list is a simple scroll region (max-height 320px), not a virtualised RecycleScroller like the product — fine for the recent-N popover; for a large/interactive notification centre, route to an obs-drawer (decisionFlow).
